differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: TiKV is a distributed, transactional key-value store designed for high availability and horizontal scalability across multiple nodes. It leverages Raft for consensus.
differences.rightDesc: RocksDB is an embeddable persistent key-value store, functioning as a library within an application. It's optimized for fast storage and local data management.

differences.title: 2. CONSENSUS
differences.leftDesc: TiKV uses the Raft consensus algorithm to ensure data consistency and fault tolerance across its distributed replicas, guaranteeing ACID transactions.
differences.rightDesc: RocksDB doesn't employ a consensus protocol as it's a single-node storage engine. Consistency relies on the application managing the data.

differences.title: 3. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: TiKV scales horizontally by adding more nodes to the cluster, increasing capacity and throughput seamlessly. Data is sharded and replicated.
differences.rightDesc: RocksDB scales vertically by upgrading the hardware of the host machine (CPU, RAM, faster disks). It's limited by the single machine's resources.

differences.title: 4. TRANSACTION SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: TiKV provides fully distributed ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) transactions across multiple keys and nodes using MVCC.
differences.rightDesc: RocksDB offers atomic batch writes and optimistic transactions within a single instance. It doesn't inherently support distributed transactions.

differences.title: 5. AVAILABILITY
differences.leftDesc: TiKV achieves high availability through data replication and Raft, ensuring that the system remains operational even if some nodes fail.
differences.rightDesc: RocksDB's availability is tied to the application hosting it. If the application or host fails, the data becomes inaccessible.

differences.title: 6. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for building distributed databases like TiDB, online transaction processing (OLTP) systems, and large-scale, mission-critical applications.
differences.rightDesc: Suitable for local storage in applications, caching, configuration management, and scenarios where a lightweight, fast embedded store is needed.

differences.title: 7. OPERATIONAL COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Managing a distributed TiKV cluster involves coordination, monitoring, and scaling multiple interconnected nodes, leading to higher operational overhead.
differences.rightDesc: RocksDB is simpler to manage as it's just a library. Deployment and upgrades are typically part of the application lifecycle.
